examples.knowledge_point: Computing a Differential in a Geometrical Context
examples.problem: Given a cone, find the differential $\textrm d V$ for the volume $V$ of the cone if the radius is $r=6$ and the height is $h = 3.$
examples.worked_solution:
The volume of the cone is $V = \dfrac{1}{3} \pi r^2h.$ Let's find the differential:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{d}V(r,h) & =(\frac{∂V}{∂r})\,\text{d}r+(\frac{∂V}{∂h})\,\text{d}h \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\pi rh\,\text{d}r+\frac{1}{3}\pi {r}^{2}\,\text{d}h.\end{aligned}
$$

For $r=6$ and $h=3,$ the differential is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{d}V(6,3) & =\frac{2}{3}\pi \cdot 6\cdot 3\,\text{d}r+\frac{1}{3}\pi \cdot {6}^{2}\,\text{d}h \\  & =12\pi \,\text{d}r+12\pi \,\text{d}h.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Find the differential $\text{d}f$ for the function $f(x,y,z)=x{e}^{-y}+y{e}^{z}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
We compute the differential using the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{d}f(x,y,z) & =(\frac{∂f}{∂x})\,\text{d}x+(\frac{∂f}{∂y})\,\text{d}y+(\frac{∂f}{∂z})\,\text{d}z \\  & =[{e}^{-y}]\,\text{d}x+[-x{e}^{-y}+{e}^{z}]\,\text{d}y+[y{e}^{z}]\,\text{d}z \\  & ={e}^{-y}\,\text{d}x+({e}^{z}-x{e}^{-y})\,\text{d}y+y{e}^{z}\,\text{d}z\end{aligned}
$$
